ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a block with mass $m{=}4\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a horizontal ground. A constant external force $F{=}10\mathrm{N}$ acts on the block at an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal direction, and the block remains stationary. The gravitational acceleration is $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The normal force and frictional force exerted by the ground on the block.
2. If the external force $F$ is gradually increased, when $F$ reaches 20N, the block is just about to slide. Assuming the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction, what is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the ground?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the block is placed on the horizontal ground; the arrow of the external force F points from near the upper end of the block toward the upper left; the dashed line represents the horizontally leftward direction, and the angle θ is marked between force F and this horizontal dashed line. Therefore, as shown in the figure, F can be decomposed into horizontally leftward F cosθ and vertically upward F sinθ. Reasoning: Given m=4 kg, g=10 m/s^2, so the weight mg=40 N. Initially F=10 N, θ=30°, and the object block is at rest. Vertical-direction equilibrium: N + F sinθ = mg, so N = mg - F sinθ = 40 - 10×sin30° = 40 - 5 = 35 N. Horizontal-direction equilibrium: the horizontal component of the external force is leftward, the static friction force of the ground on the object block is rightward, and the magnitude f = F cosθ = 10×cos30° = 5√3 N. When F increases to 20 N, the object block is just about to slide. At this time, the maximum static friction force is equal to the horizontal component of the external force: f_max = 20 cos30° = 10√3 N. In the vertical direction there is still N = mg - F sinθ = 40 - 20×sin30° = 40 - 10 = 30 N. From f_max = μN, get μ = f_max/N = 10√3/30 = √3/3. The problem states that the maximum static friction equals sliding friction, so the kinetic friction coefficient μ_k = √3/3.

As shown in the figure, a block with mass $m=4\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on horizontal ground. A constant external force $F=10\mathrm{N}$ acts on the block at an angle of $\theta=30^\circ$ to the horizontal, and the block remains stationary. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

method.method_draft: Draw a free-body diagram using the figure: the block rests on a horizontal floor, and the applied force arrow is directed up and to the left, making angle θ with the horizontal dashed line. From the text use m=4 kg, g=10 m/s^2, θ=30°, initial F=10 N, and later limiting F=20 N. Resolve F into components: horizontal F cosθ leftward and vertical F sinθ upward. Since the block is stationary, impose ΣFx=0 and ΣFy=0. Vertically, N+F sinθ=mg, so N=mg-F sinθ. Horizontally, static friction must oppose the leftward component, so f=F cosθ to the right. Substitute F=10 N for part 1. For part 2, at impending sliding with F=20 N, use f_max=F cosθ and N=mg-F sinθ, then μ_k=μ_s,max=f_max/N.

method.method_draft: Treat the ground's total contact force as a single resultant R made of a normal component N and a tangential friction component f. From the image, the applied force points up-left, so the combined effect of weight plus applied force must be balanced by a ground reaction pointing up-right relative to the block. Use vector equilibrium R + mg downward + F inclined up-left = 0. Therefore the horizontal component of R equals F cosθ to the right, which is the friction magnitude, and the vertical component of R equals mg-F sinθ, which is the normal force. Insert F=10 N for the first part. For the second part with F=20 N just before motion, the contact resultant lies on the edge of the friction cone, so μ equals the ratio of its tangential component to its normal component: μ=(F cosθ)/(mg-F sinθ).

推理：方块静止，竖直方向不能加速，所以竖直方向受力平衡。重力 mg=4×10=40 N 向下，外力竖直分量 F sinθ 向上，地面对方块的支持力 N 向上，因此 N+F sinθ=mg，即 N=mg-F sinθ。代入 F=10 N、θ=30°，得 N=40-10×1/2=35 N。水平方向也静止，外力水平分量 F cosθ 向左，所以地面对方块的静摩擦力必须向右，大小 f=F cosθ=10×√3/2=5√3 N。
当 F 增大到 20 N 时，方块刚要滑动，此时所需摩擦力达到最大值。此时支持力 N=mg-F sinθ=40-20×1/2=30 N；水平拉力分量为 F cosθ=20×√3/2=10√3 N。由最大静摩擦等于滑动摩擦，μ_k N=F cosθ，所以 μ_k=(10√3)/30=√3/3。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read that the applied force is above the horizontal and points leftward, so it both unloads the normal force and demands rightward friction; read that the support is a flat horizontal ground.
planner_metadata.text_role: Provides all numerical quantities and the condition that at F=20 N the block is just about to slide, with maximum static friction equal to sliding friction.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use rigid-body equilibrium under constraints: zero vertical motion fixes N, zero horizontal motion fixes static friction, and impending slip occurs when required friction equals μN.

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, a block with mass $m=4\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on horizontal ground. A constant external force $F=10\mathrm{N}$ acts on the block at an angle of $\theta=30^\circ$ to the horizontal, and the block remains stationary. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

1. Find the normal force and the frictional force exerted by the ground on the block.
2. If the external force $F$ is gradually increased, when $F$ reaches $20\mathrm{N}$, the block is just about to slide. Assuming the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction, find the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the ground.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the block is placed on the horizontal ground; the arrow of the external force F points from near the upper end of the block toward the upper left; the dashed line represents the horizontally leftward direction, and the angle θ is marked between force F and this horizontal dashed line. Therefore, as shown in the figure, F can be decomposed into horizontally leftward F cosθ and vertically upward F sinθ.
Reasoning: Given m=4 kg, g=10 m/s^2, so the weight mg=40 N. Initially F=10 N, θ=30°, and the object block is at rest. Vertical-direction equilibrium: N + F sinθ = mg, so N = mg - F sinθ = 40 - 10×sin30° = 40 - 5 = 35 N. Horizontal-direction equilibrium: the horizontal component of the external force is leftward, the static friction force of the ground on the object block is rightward, and the magnitude f = F cosθ = 10×cos30° = 5√3 N.
When F increases to 20 N, the object block is just about to slide. At this time, the maximum static friction force is equal to the horizontal component of the external force: f_max = 20 cos30° = 10√3 N. In the vertical direction there is still N = mg - F sinθ = 40 - 20×sin30° = 40 - 10 = 30 N. From f_max = μN, get μ = f_max/N = 10√3/30 = √3/3. The problem states that the maximum static friction equals sliding friction, so the kinetic friction coefficient μ_k = √3/3.
